fact: The CEMAC regulation of 21 December 2018 on payment services replaced the 2011 e-money rules, which had covered e-money issuance only, and is the framework under which Chad's payment establishments are licensed (L'Economie, 29 July 2026).

Moov Money Tchad SA, a telecom subsidiary, holds a COBAC payment-establishment licence with FCFA 500 million minimum paid-up capital, confirmed in Maroc Telecom's half-year report of 22 July 2026, the third non-bank in Chad so licensed.
Airtel Money in Chad was licensed as a payment establishment by COBAC in 2023, and the fintech Konoom in 2025, per the article.

In Chad, Airtel Mobile Commerce was the only licensed payment establishment reporting to COBAC for 2025, with net banking income up 64.2% to FCFA 4.4 billion and 361 million operations (COBAC 2025 annual report, via Ecomatin, 9 October 2026; report date not stated).

BEAC's register of instructions, circulars and regulations lists CEMAC/UMAC Regulation No. 03 of 21 December 2016 on payment systems, means and incidents as a CEMAC-wide text; Chad is a CEMAC member. Document published date used (2026-09-02) for the register; instrument dated 2016.
